_comment: The club's commercial offer, and the only place it is written down.
The API serves it to the offer page, the invoice uses it for line items,
and tools/sync_tiers.py writes it into the landing page, so these numbers
cannot drift between what a visitor is shown and what they are charged.
THE TASTING CASE IS THE ONE TIER THAT CHARGES FOR CARRIAGE. $120 for the
wine and $40 for the shipping, Cecilia's decision in November 2026: the
winery does not absorb freight on a three-bottle box, because freight
does not fall as fast as the bottle count. Her arithmetic holds — strip
the carriage out of the other two and their wine is $36.67 and $39.25 a
bottle, against $40 here.
The $40 is the dearest ground zone for three bottles, so no member is
subsidised by the winery. A West Coast member pays about $4 more than
their box costs, and an ice pack in the warm months costs $5 that this
does not cover. Charging each member their own zone instead is a change
to _create_order, not to this file.
The name is still a placeholder.
NUMBERS NEED THE WINERY'S SIGN-OFF, and these are Cecilia's, given in
October 2026: $275.00 for six bottles and $550.00 for twelve, both with
shipping included and neither carrying a standing discount — that was
withdrawn from the offer on 19 October, and discount_pct is left at zero
rather than deleted so the field is there if it comes back. Two earlier
tiers are gone — The Cellar Door (4 bottles at $180) in October 2026, and
The Inner Circle, the by-invitation tier, with this change. Nothing in
the code assumes a tier is invite-only or is not; the mechanism is still
there for the day one comes back.
Every tier includes shipping, so an order raises a single line; the
shipping line and its QuickBooks item only come back if a tier charges
for carriage again.
Three shipments a year now, not two: spring, fall and Christmas. The
months are what the despatch screens count from. Nothing bills on an
interval any more: a member saves a card when they join and the club
charges it when a release goes out, so these three dates are the whole
calendar and there is no second one inside Stripe to keep in step.
